γεωργία καὶ εἴ τι χειροποίητον, φησὶ διαπεπετασμένας καὶ οὐ συνεστραμμένας οὐδὲ
τὸ πρέπον ἔργον χερσὶ ποιουμένας, ὡς ἐν ἀργῷ καὶ ἐρήμῳ τῇ χώρᾳ. εἰ δὲ τοὺς ἐν
οικοῦντας λέγει, χεῖρες ἂν εἶεν γεωργοὶ καὶ ἐργάται, μὴ συστέλλοντες εἰς ἔργα τὰς
χεῖρας διὰ τὰ περιστάντα. εἰ δὲ τῆς Σιὼν χεῖρες τρο πολογοῦνται, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὰ
κατὰ τὴν γραφὴν μέλη τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ ὄρος, ὡς εἰπεῖν, μετὰ τοῦ ἔθνους
στενάζει, οὐκ ἔχον εἰς παραμυθίαν οὐ θεόν, οὐχ ἅγιον ἄνδρα. 38 Στόμα κυρίου τοὺς
προφήτας ἐκληπτέον, ὧν ὑπάρχων Ἡσαΐας ἔλεγε· «τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησε
ταῦτα». Ἱερουσαλὴμ δὲ ὠνεί δισται ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος ὡς «ἀποκτείνασα τοὺς
προφήτας», καθὸ καὶ παρεπίκρανε τὸ στόμα κυρίου πόνοις αὐτοὺς πικροτάτοις
ἐκδοῦσα. ὁ δὲ «τὸ αἷμα τῶν προφητῶν ἐκζητῶν» θεὸς ἀλγηδόσι ταῖς ἐκ πολέμων καὶ
πάλιν αἰχμαλωσίαις παραδίδωσιν αὐτῆς νεα νίσκους τε καὶ παρθένους . ἀνθ' ὧν οὖν
πέπονθεν, ἐξομολογεῖται τοῖς ἄλλοις ἑαυτὴ
pass_a_gloss: He notes farming and crafts lie unused, hands idle like barren fields. Those inside would work fields, not pull back due to trouble. But Zion’s hands? Far more—Scripture’s members of God. Even the mountain mourns with its folk, no God, no holy one to soothe. Heed the Lord’s mouth in prophets: Isaiah states it spoke these words. Jerusalem, praised by Savior as prophet-killer, yet angered the Lord’s mouth, handing them to bitter fate. The God seeking prophets’ blood gives her war’s pains and captivity—youths and maids taken. For this she admits fault, offers herself as warning to others who learned God’s right, lest they repeat. Beyond senses: virgins = pure-livers, youths = virtuous achievers. Saints often share guilt of the accountable. Ezekiel names Jerusalem’s lovers—Olivet—saying Lord will rouse them: Babylon’s sons, all Chaldeans, around. Once friends by God’s care, now foes. Love frequently turns to hate; he notes Samaria’s Oholah whoring from him, embracing Assyrian lovers, then given over to them. He adds Jerusalem’s Oholibah saw, outdid her sister’s harlotry, and threw herself on Assyrian sons. 41 Prophecy makes the soul ache as if convinced of clear truth; but Lamentation, now that these events occurred, mourns bitterly and admits through sin that she brought God’s kindness to utter bitterness upon herself—like a once-teeming mother made childless, facing war’s dread hand. No real city with fertile womb and broken heart is meant by the personification. 42 He splits the discourse into eight: Jerusalem speaks to foes he wants hearing, and to God. What does he prompt enemies to hear? What does he tell God about them, as if they rejoiced? Maybe because her and Israel’s guilt taught nations to envy them, and when Gentile fullness enters, all Israel saved—thus he first addresses nations mystically, then God about later points: “You were abandoned to suffer so you’d gain the land; I became God’s foe through you, though chosen and beloved for the fathers’ sake, I still endure.” You hear my groaning and know why: I am utterly spent for your salvation, abandoned, lacking my constant comforter in affliction. The ruler from Judah’s line, the hope of nations, the stored blessing—gone; his blood cries for vengeance, yet no one comforts Jerusalem. Do not let their evil go unpunished; let your oversight be like praying for wounds to see a doctor, seeking full cure. The whole blessing: first, not sinning; second, God examining all our wickedness. Glean the leftover grapes after harvest, as the poor do—just as you once cleaned my vines, stripping every worthless tendril, even the bitter cluster—so let me glean my foes. If they were fully saved with me, I, by your judgment, Lord, would gain salvation’s verdict; I see them and am pierced with grief, self-condemned, needing your oversight. Like David’s word: He will shatter all sinners’ horns. Now he means the rulers, where the nation’s strength lies…
pass_b_english:
Agriculture and any handiwork, he says, are left spread out and not gathered together, failing to perform the proper work with their hands, as if in an idle and desolate land. If, however, he is speaking of those dwelling within, the hands would be farmers and laborers, not withdrawing their hands from work due to surrounding circumstances. But if the hands of Zion are being counted, how much more the members according to Scripture of God are to be regarded. And indeed, the mountain itself, as it were, groans with the people, lacking comfort from God or from a holy man. The mouth of the Lord must be heeded in the prophets, of whom Isaiah, who exists, declared: "For the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things." Yet Jerusalem, rewarded by the Savior as "having slain the prophets," moreover, provoked the mouth of the Lord to bitter pains by delivering them over. But the God who "seeks the blood of the prophets" delivers her to afflictions from wars and again to captivities, handing over her young men and virgins. Therefore, for what she has suffered, she confesses before others, presenting herself as an example to these, so that those who have learned God’s righteousness may not suffer similar things. After the perceptible, interpret virgins as those living in incorruptibility, and young men as those prospering in virtue. For often the holy ones also suffer with those responsible. The lovers, namely those who are such, Ezekiel has declared to Jerusalem, whom he calls Olivet, saying: "Thus says the Lord Lord: Behold, I will stir up your lovers against you from every side, sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans." For these, though formerly friends by divine providence, have turned into enemies.

It often happens, under the impulse of love, that one turns into hatred; for he speaks concerning Samaria thus: “And Oholah played the harlot away from me, and she set herself upon her lovers, the Assyrians”; and shortly after: “Therefore he delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the sons of Assyria.” He also speaks concerning Jerusalem: “And her sister Oholibah saw it, and she defiled her illicit affection more than the harlotry of her sister, and she set herself upon the sons of the Assyrians.” 41 In the prophecy, indeed, the soul grieves as if being persuaded of obvious things; but in the present Lamentation, as though these things have already come to pass, she grieves bitterly and, through sin, confesses that she has brought upon herself the utmost bitterness of God’s goodness, as if she, who was abundantly fruitful, had been made barren, and as if the most terrible thing—war by hostile hand—had befallen her. Since personification is employed, one should not seek a literal city whose womb bore children and whose heart was loosened. 42 He divides the word into eight parts, addressing Jerusalem toward her enemies, whom he wishes to hear, and toward God. But what does he urge upon the enemies for their hearing? And what does he say to God about them, as if they had rejoiced? Perhaps, therefore (since “her transgression and Israel’s transgression have become the instruction of the nations to provoke them to jealousy,” and “when the fullness of the nations has entered in, then all Israel will be saved”), he speaks prophetically first to those from the nations, and then to God concerning the second matters: “You were left behind to suffer so that you might take possession of the land, and I have become, through you, an enemy of God, though according to the election, beloved for the sake of the fathers, I continue to exist.”

Therefore, you have heard my lamentation and perceived its cause; for I am entirely consumed on account of your salvation, left bereft, lacking the one who continually comforts me amid the trials of evil. Now the "leader has departed from Judah, and he who was reckoned from his loins" has come—He to whom belonged "the things stored up," "the expectation of the nations"—at whose blood’s vengeance, no one remains to console Jerusalem. This means: let not their wickedness be allowed to persist unchecked; rather, may it be granted to you in oversight, as if one were to pray for wounds to come before a physician, in order to attain complete healing. For this is the whole: blessed above all is the one who does not sin, and second, blessed is the one whom God examines wholly for wickedness. Moreover, glean after the vintage the small remnants of the grape clusters left behind, as the poor do. Just as when you carefully inspected my vines, you cleansed them, removing every worthless shoot down to the tiniest bits—“the cluster of gall and the bunch of bitterness”—so too, let me glean after my enemies. This would be beneficial to me, for if they were fully saved alongside me, then I, according to your judgment, O Lord, would obtain salvation’s verdict; whom I see, I am deeply grieved and condemn myself, the oversight I need from you. Likewise, as David said: “He will utterly crush all the horns of the sinners.” Now he speaks of the rulers, in whom resides the strength of the nation…
